18 Then certain philosophers of the Epicureans, and of the Stoicks, encountered him. And some said, What will this babbler say? other some, He seemeth to be a setter forth of strange gods: because he preached unto them Jesus, and the resurrection. - Acts 17:18 (KJV)

 Paul was in Athens, and these Greek philosophers were meeting daily to hear any new doctrine, or about any new Gods. Paul met with them, and started teaching Jesus to them, and they were interested for awhile. This same attitude is in the world today, and so many carnal people think that Christians are just babblers, and don’t make any sense. We need to all be like Paul, and tell the Gospel to any, and all, that will listen to us. Paul was also teaching the Jews (Acts 17:17) in the synagogue, as he was prone to do everywhere he went. Paul was so on fire for God, that he would teach to anyone who was around, and we should take a lesson from him.

 Paul was knowledgeable about Greek literature, and he used the fact that they believed in an unknown god (Acts 17:23), along with many others, and he told them that the true God was the unknown god they had an alter for. We need to learn from Paul, and find ways to make Jesus interesting to those who don’t know Him. One way is to make Jesus relative to their lives, whether it is by healing their bodies, financial, peace, joy, etc., we need to make our Jesus appeal to their lives now, and not just in the future. If we would teach the full Gospel of Jesus, it would include healing, financial, and all the fruit of the Spirit (Galatians 5:22-23). Most unsaved people are lacking in joy and peace in their lives, and it is because they don’t have the Spirit of God living in them, and they look for relief through drugs, alcohol, sex, etc. Let Christ live through you, and let your light shine (Matthew 5:16), so that people will want what you have, and then be sure and tell them about Jesus. Let’s all shine, so we will light up this dark world – Praise God.

The point of taking money out of politics, at least as I understand it, is taking money out of the campaign and election side of things. Politicians are bought because of big money donations by corporations. The feeling is that by stopping these donations from being made in the first place a politician will be less likely to make shitty laws for the sake of their corporate backers.

But why does the money lead to elections? It's advertising dollars. It's paying staffers around the country. It's setting up campaign trail events. Take the money out of politics and you're left with the super rich being the only ones able to finance a viable campaign.
That's the downside of the "Get money out" campaign. The only middle ground would be something that discourages corporations from donating but that would also lead to a lack of funding.
OK... what criteria do we use to decide who gets money?

Because these politicians who gained power in the first place through the donations of certain special interest groups would then cease to have any sort of burden to "repay" these groups, that got them elected in the first place, by supporting laws that favor their business interests.
It isn't possible to remove money from politics. The two are inextricably related. It's like saying let's get the resources out of the allocation of resources.
